text:
maria: Hey team — our JS sample app deployed to Vercel Edge started failing after the SDK bump to v2.3.0. Build log shows a couple errors: `Error: Cannot use import statement outside a module` and `Error: ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find module 'redwood-inference'` when code does `const RI = require('redwood-inference')`. Anyone hit this?

dev-bot: CI: samples/integration-edge — job #1245 failed on esm/cjs-interop test. See logs: `build › bundle › fail on require/import interop`.

lee: Yep — this is coming from the new conditional `exports` map we shipped in 2.3.0. Current package.json in the SDK looks like:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
On normal Node this is fine, but on edge runtimes the bundler/optimizer sometimes resolves to the wrong conditional branch (or treats package as ESM-only). For some legacy sample apps that still call `require('redwood-inference')` the runtime ends up trying to load the ESM build and throws.

sam: Repro steps I used: `git checkout samples/edge && npm i redwood-inference@2.3.0 && vercel dev`. Error appears when the dev server bundles it for edge. Workaround I found: change to `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` or use dynamic import: `const RI = await import('redwood-inference')` — but both require changing sample code.

oliver: We also have a TypeScript typing issue: TS picks up `types` pointing at the ESM `index.d.ts` and when downstream code expects a CJS `module.exports` shape it ends up with `.default` mismatches. The conditional `types`/`typings` entry is missing. We should add conditional types exports so TS can pick the right shape depending on import style.

maria: For context, this is breaking onboarding for a bunch of quickstarts that still use `require()` in examples. Devs hit a confusing stack trace and open support tickets. We should decide whether to patch the SDK to be edge-friendly or update all samples.

lee: Proposal: quick patch release that reintroduces a fallback path and adds a `worker` condition in exports. Something like:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "node": { "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js", "import": "./dist/node/esm/index.js" },
    "worker": "./dist/edge/esm/index.js",
    "default": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
That should help Vite/Esbuild/Vercel pick the edge esm build while letting plain Node `require` keep resolving. Also add a `types` conditional: `"types": { "worker": "dist/edge/index.d.ts", "default": "dist/cjs/index.d.ts" }`.

sam: Small note: some bundlers ignore non-standard conditions. Also `default` condition isn't part of the conditional exports spec — but many packagers look for a fallback. We need to test against Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge, and LAmbda@Edge.

oliver: Another approach is to ship an explicit `dist/edge` entry and update samples that target edge to `import 'redwood-inference/edge'` (explicit subpath). That avoids relying on resolver heuristics. Example: `import RI from 'redwood-inference/edge'` where `exports` includes `"./edge": "./dist/edge/esm/index.js"`.

maria: I like that since it's explicit and documents the migration path. But we still need a patch for users who don't change sample code. Can we do both?

lee: I'll open a hotfix PR: 1) add `./edge` subpath export, 2) add `worker` conditional mapping, 3) add conditional `types` entries, 4) add a revert-like fallback so `require()` doesn't accidentally resolve to an ESM file. I'll also add integration tests that run `vercel` and `wrangler` builds in CI matrix.

dev-bot: GitHub Actions: opened job #2304 — "add edge exports + tests" by lee. CI matrix will include `platform: node, vercel, cloudflare` on PR.

sam: For docs/sample update: change sample-app package.json and README to prefer `import` for edge templates and show fallback for older Node: `const RI = require('redwood-inference').default || require('redwood-inference')`. Also add a short note in migration guide: "If you hit import/require errors after upgrading, try the explicit `/edge` subpath or update to the import form."

oliver: Also add a small unit test in the SDK that runs `node -e "console.log(require('redwood-inference')?.version)"` in a CJS process and `node --input-type=module -e "import('redwood-inference').then(m=>console.log(m.version))"` for ESM — to avoid regressions.

maria: Thanks. Action items: @lee open PR and assign to @oliver for export map review, @sam to update samples/edge, @maria to file docs issue and coordinate support notif. I'll write a short blurb for changelog and customer comms.

lee: Will do. ETA: PR today, patch release if green.

maria: Great — once PR is merged let's run the sample deploys and close the support tickets. :thumbsup:

sam: Also adding a smoke test to the onboarding flow that deploys sample to Vercel preview in CI so we catch this earlier.

oliver: Sounds good. Thanks all.

maria: Closing loop here — please ping if you need help reproducing specific customer stack traces.
